subject.title: [Feature]: 内置健壮性机制：Watchdog、全局错误处理、自动恢复

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in Gateway watchdog and recovery ladder, and which recovery actions are allowed by default versus explicit opt-in?
rationale: The issue adds core recovery semantics, config surface, degraded startup behavior, possible state/config mutation, and operator notifications that require product and security intent before implementation.

options.title: Keep as design umbrella
options.body: Use this issue to settle the core recovery policy, then review narrower PRs and issues such as crash ladder, rescue watchdog, health probes, and doctor auto-fix against that design.

options.title: Split and close later
options.body: Move each remaining slice to a specific canonical issue and close this only after the broad context is preserved there.

options.title: Reject core ownership
options.body: Document that recovery belongs to external supervisors, plugins, or ClawHub packages instead of adding core watchdog semantics.

recommendation.title: Keep as design umbrella
recommendation.body: Use this issue to settle the core recovery policy, then review narrower PRs and issues such as crash ladder, rescue watchdog, health probes, and doctor auto-fix against that design.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal is recent current-main ownership across the Gateway crash-loop breaker, health monitor, and process error-handling paths.
